name: Dhra raised-floor granary
description: At Dhra in the Jordan Valley, a purpose-built structure interpreted as a granary had a suspended floor supported above ground, enabling food storage.

impact.note: One community's early purpose-built granary, showing stored surplus before farming, a real new ability there that later storage buildings continued.

date.label: Approximately 11,300–11,200 cal BP (9350–9250 BCE)
date.basis: Authors estimate construction of Structure 4 phase I at approximately 11,300–11,200 cal BP, from stratigraphy and radiocarbon context; the conversion uses 1950 as BP reference.

events.statement: At Dhra in the Jordan Valley, a purpose-built structure interpreted as a granary had a suspended floor supported above ground, enabling food storage.
events.caveats: The floor and use are archaeological reconstructions; claims about ownership and storage duration are hypotheses. The date refers to phase I at one structure.

evidence.supports: Authors interpret Structure 4 as a raised-floor granary, with phase I construction approximately 11,300–11,200 cal BP.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest evidence currently researched for this scoped record; not a claim of global priority. The floor and use are archaeological reconstructions; claims about ownership and storage duration are hypotheses. The date refers to phase I at one structure.

caveats: The floor and use are archaeological reconstructions; claims about ownership and storage duration are hypotheses. The date refers to phase I at one structure.
